'''''Euonymus fortunei''''', the '''spindle''', '''Fortune's spindle''', '''winter creeper''' or '''wintercreeper''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Celastraceae, [[native plant|native]] to east Asia, including China, Korea, the Philippines and Japan.<ref name="china-fortunei"/> ''E. fortunei'' is highly invasive and damaging in the [[United States]], causing the death of trees and forest in urban areas.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://moinvasives.org/2019/08/15/you-should-be-concerned-when-this-plant-goes-vertical/|title= You Should Be Concerned When This Plant Goes Vertical|work=Missouri invade plants task force|date=August 15, 2019|access-date=November 28, 2020}}</ref>

==Description==
It is an [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] which grows as a [[vine]] if provided with support.  As such, it grows to {{convert|20|m|0|abbr=on}}, climbing by means of small rootlets on the stems, similar to [[ivy]] (an example of [[convergent evolution]], as the two species are not related). Like ivy, it also has a sterile non-flowering [[juvenile (organism)|juvenile]] climbing or creeping phase, which on reaching high enough into the crowns of trees to get more light, develops into an adult, flowering phase without climbing rootlets.

The [[leaf|leaves]] are arranged in opposite pairs, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 2–6 cm long and 1–3 cm broad, with finely serrated margins. The [[flower]]s are inconspicuous, 5 mm in diameter, with four small greenish-yellow petals. The [[fruit]] is a smooth, [[Dehiscence (botany)|dehiscent capsule]] with reddish [[aril]]s.<ref name="Zouhar">{{cite web|last=Zouhar|first=Kris|date=2009|title= Euonymus fortunei. In: Fire Effects Information System|publisher=U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service |url=https://www.fs.fed.us/database/feis/plants/vine/euofor/all.html|access-date=February 14, 2020}}</ref>

''Euonymus fortunei'' is very similar to ''[[Euonymus japonicus]]'', particularly in cultivation. In the wild, ''E. fortunei'' is climbing or procumbent whereas ''E. japonicus'' has an erect habit.<ref name=FoC/>

== Taxonomy ==
The species was described in 1863 as  ''Elaeodendron fortunei'' by [[Nikolai Turczaninow]],<ref name=":0">{{APNI2|id=124464|name=''Euonymus fortunei''|access-date=2023-09-29}}</ref> who named it in honour of the Scottish botanist and plant explorer [[Robert Fortune]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Turczaninow, P.K.N.S.|author-link=Porphir Kiril Nicolai Stepanowitsch Turczaninow|date=1863|title=Eleodendron Fortunei|journal= Bulletin de la Société Impériale des Naturalistes de Moscou|volume= 36|issue=1|page=602|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/44325452#page/663}}</ref> The species had already been described as ''Euonymus hederaceus'' in 1851; Turczaninow's name is [[Conserved name|conserved]] against this earlier name.<ref name=IPNI_160669-1>{{IPNI|taxon=''Elaeodendron fortunei'' |authority=Turcz..|id=160669-1|access-date=2024-11-08|mode=cs1}}</ref><ref name="china-fortunei"/> It was transferred from ''Elaeodendron'' to the genus ''[[Euonymus]]'' in 1933 by [[Heinrich von Handel-Mazzetti]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite book|author=Handel-Mazzetti, H. |date=1933|title=Symbolae Sinicae, Botanische Ergebnisse der Expedition der Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien nach Sudwest-China 1914/1918|volume= 7|issue=3|page= 660|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/733783}} </ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It has an extensive native range, including many parts of China (from sea level to 3400 m elevation), India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Laos, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam.<ref name="china-fortunei">{{cite web | url = http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200012800 | work = Flora of China | title = Euonymus fortunei (Turczaninow) Handel-Mazzetti |access-date=2024-11-08}}</ref> It has also been introduced to North America as an ornamental, and is considered an invasive species throughout much of the Eastern United States.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Winter Creeper {{!}} University of Maryland Extension |url=https://extension.umd.edu/resource/winter-creeper |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=extension.umd.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Wintercreeper Control |url=https://mdc.mo.gov/trees-plants/invasive-plants/wintercreeper-control |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=Missouri Department of Conservation |language=en}}</ref>  It resembles ''[[Euonymus japonicus]]'', which is also widely cultivated but is a shrub, without climbing roots.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200012806 | work = Flora of China | title = Euonymus japonicus Thunberg }}</ref>  It also is related to a variety of similar species, including ''Euonymus theifolius'', or ''Euonymus vagans'' and also a number of named "species" which are found only in cultivation and better treated as cultivars.<ref name="china-fortunei" /> Its habitats include woodlands, scrub, and forests.<ref name="china-fortunei"/>

==Cultivation==
''Euonymus fortunei'' is widely cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]], with numerous [[cultivar]]s selected for such traits as yellow, [[variegation|variegated]] and slow, [[dwarfing|dwarfed]] growth. It is used as a [[groundcover]] or a vine to climb walls and trees. The following cultivars have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 37 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 18 February 2018}}</ref>
* 'Emerald Gaiety'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Euonymus fortunei'' 'Emerald Gaiety'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/97545/Euonymus-fortunei-Emerald-Gaiety-(v)/Details | access-date = 7 June 2020}}</ref>
* 'Emerald 'n' Gold'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Euonymus fortunei'' 'Emerald 'n' Gold'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/96928/Euonymus-fortunei-Emerald-n-Gold-(v)/Details | access-date = 7 June 2020}}</ref>
* 'Emerald Surprise'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Euonymus fortunei'' 'Emerald Surprise'|url=
https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/51080/Euonymus-fortunei-Emerald-Surprise-(v)/Details | access-date = 7 June 2020}}</ref>
* 'Kewensis'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/98830/Euonymus-fortunei-Kewensis/Details | title = ''Euonymus fortunei'' 'Kewensis' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 23 June 2020}}</ref>
* 'Wolong Ghost'<ref>{{cite web | url =  https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/191101/Euonymus-fortunei-Wolong-Ghost/Details | title = ''Euonymus fortunei'' 'Wolong Ghost' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 23 June 2020}}</ref>

Plants propagated from mature flowering stems (formerly sometimes named "f. ''carrierei''") always grow as non-climbing [[shrub]]s. Some popular cultivars such as 'Moon Shadow' are shrub forms.

Most of the cultivated plants belong to var. ''radicans'' (Huxley 1992). It is generally considered cold hardy in [[hardiness zone|USDA zones]] 5 to 9, and is considered an [[invasive species]] in some parts of the world, notably the eastern United States<ref name=plants>{{ cite web |url=http://www.plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=EUFOR2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060527132445/http://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=EUFOR2 |archive-date=May 27, 2006 |title=Profile for ''Euonymus fortunei'' (Turcz.)
